newsitem.title: USA: Kemp says Clinton's Iraq policy vague.
newsitem.headline: Kemp says Clinton's Iraq policy vague.

text.p: Republican vice presidential nominee Jack Kemp attacked President Bill Clinton's Iraq policy on Wednesday as "vague and uncertain" and said Clinton should clarify it before taking further action there.

In a written statement issued to reporters travelling with Republican presidential nominee Bob Dole, Kemp reacted to the latest events in the Gulf, where Iraqis fired a missile at two U.S. F-16 jets on Wednesday.
"Our alliances are in disarray and support for our mission is at risk because President Clinton's policy is vague and uncertain," Kemp said.
"Before any further action the president must clearly state his policies, forthrightly explain his objectives, and tell us how he intends to implement these goals," he said.

"In what is obviously a worsening situation, the public will only stand united behind the president if he plainly explains his policies and tells the American people what is required to achieve them," Kemp said.

The U.S. planes were not damaged in the early morning attack. The Clinton administration responded by warning that Iraq would soon learn Washington was "not playing games" and that firing missiles at U.S. planes would draw a response "disproportionate" to the Iraqi attack.
Dole, who was campaigning on Wednesday in Connecticut and Delaware, did not immediately comment on the latest developments in Iraq.

But two days ago Dole chided Clinton for claiming success in a showdown with Iraq, saying "events on the ground" contradicted the statement. Dole challenged Clinton's claim that the cruise missile strikes the president ordered last week had achieved their purpose.
Kemp said there were several objectives that must be met before the U.S. Iraqi mission could be considered a success.

He said Iraqi leader Saddam Hussein must withdraw his troops and security agents from northern Iraq, cease his support of international terrorism, cooperate fully with the U.N. weapons inspection, and release Kurdish prisoners and stop brutality against the Kurdish people.
"As of today, it is apparent that none of these objectives have been met," Kemp said.
